findings.evidence: Digest at dbff837f is a cut list: 'removed units (111, showing 40)'. Each of the 40 shown para ids maps through sections.json (s001-s032) to a record row with an allowed (fate, value, decision) combination, and no drop row covers substantive content. The other 71 units were not listed in the digest, so they could only be checked through the section rows.
findings.fix: Rerun the digest without truncation, or list all 111 para ids, so each unit can be matched to its record row directly. If a unit has no covering section row, add a row for it to docs/audit/recovery/domain-name-brainstormer/record.md. Content stays where it is.

findings.evidence: Procedure step 5 holds the label definitions, the curl command, a classification table and one very long WHOIS-fallback paragraph ('WHOIS fallback for a TLD without RDAP (...): `timeout 20 whois -h whois.iana.org <tld>` ... never retry in a loop. For each checked name record the source ...'). The tool-style lookup procedure sits inside the process list and breaks its rhythm.
findings.fix: Split the WHOIS-fallback paragraph into short numbered sub-steps: IANA lookup, then the registry server query, then the reply-to-label mapping, then the no-tool and throttle fallbacks. Keep every fact and every date in SKILL.md step 5 and drop nothing.

findings.evidence: Six evals cover defaults, bilingual screening, honest status, pasted RDAP, budget without a quote and the sample. None covers Procedure step 4 ('When the first choice is taken'), even though the description triggers on 'replacing a taken first choice' and trigger-queries.json has a Rosie's Crumb Co. query for it. Eval ids 'casual-climate-names' and 'short-ai-names' also do not match their prompts.
findings.fix: Add an eval with a prompt such as 'rosiescrumb.com is registered by a local wedding florist; should we use rosiescrumb.co or pick a new name?'. Assert that the answer applies step 4's keep-or-rename test and warns that traffic and email typed to .com will reach the holder. Rename the two ids to match their prompts, for example 'casual-energy-names' and 'bilingual-learning-names'.

findings.evidence: The example cuts 'sharecode' because it 'reads as two common words, so it is hard to tell apart from others'. That is not one of Procedure step 2's cut criteria (more than one plausible spelling, an unwanted meaning or sound, an established same-category brand nearby), so an agent following the example applies a rule SKILL.md does not state.
findings.fix: Restate the sharecode cut in terms of a step 2 criterion, for example 'sharecode (an established same-category brand nearby, like codeshare)'. Alternatively, add 'too generic to stand out among same-category names' to step 2's cut list in SKILL.md so the example and the procedure agree.
